title: Changes in enums are not detected in @export var
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads)

### Issue description

I have an enum "my_enum" in an autoload. Let's say it has 3 entries:
entry_01, entry_02 and entry_03.

Elsewhere, some scenes have an `@export` var "E" that reflects the enum like this:
`@export var E : Autoload.my_enum = Autoload.my_enum.entry01`
and I can select any of the three entries for E. This part works as expected.

But, when I change the enum by, say, adding entry_04, I can't select entry_04 as a value "E" for the scene that connects to the enum through `@export`.

The only way for me to set enum_04 as a value for E is to restart Godot. This works, but then as soon as I add another key to the enum (or rename an existing one) in the Autoload I have to restart Godot again for the changes to propagate.

### Steps to reproduce

Download the MRP.
In the only scene that opens, locate the "enum_test" node in the ProjectTree and click on it.
In the Inspector, confirm you can set the "enum_test"'s "E" to any of the three entries.
Locate and open the "autoload.gd" script in the FileSystem panel.
Edit the enum so it has 4 entries, for example call the new addition "entry04".
Save the "autoload.gd" script.
Go back to the "enum_test" node and try to change the "E" to the new (fourth) entry "entry04". It will be missing from the list. You will only see  "entry01",  "entry02" and "entry03".

…close and reload the project. Now you will be able to change the "E" to "entry04".

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[bug-test-update-enum.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20676919/bug-test-update-enum.zip)
